The AA specializations must retain the note’s stated restriction to the same full endpoint component. I recommend two small wording clarifications at the end of this report; neither changes the mathematics.This is an audit of the supplied written proofs and Lean statements. The direction tag proves injection for all neutral01 contactsLocation: New note, §§1–2.The essential point is that the tag is an owner-level direction assigned to endpoint positions. It is not the local tangent direction at every endpoint.For each original phase01 U owner  $O$ , let  $\tau(O)$  be the direction from either terminal toward its bar. Both terminals have this same direction, including when the two legal leg heights differ. Assign  $\tau(O)$  to every original endpoint of  $O$ . Original endpoint disjointness makes this a well-defined function on the union of phase01 endpoint sets.Consequently, if two endpoint stencils require different tags at the same lattice position, there are only two possibilities:They belong to the same original owner, contradicting that owner’s single tag.They belong to different original owners, contradicting original endpoint disjointness.This argument explicitly permits an owner to recur at multiple contacts.The eight-frame argument is exhaustive at arbitrary dimensionsFor a contact with forced position  $z$  and frame  $(s,d)$ , the required active-owner endpoints are
$$z-s-d,\qquad z-d,\qquad z+s-d,$$
all tagged  $s$ . The required passive-owner endpoints are
$$z-s,\qquad z-s+d,$$
both tagged  $d$ .The active stencil uses the terminal and its first two predecessors. Legal height at least four supplies these endpoints, including at the minimum height. The passive stencil uses its terminal and first predecessor. Enlarging either height or the width does not remove any stencil point. Thus there is no dimension cutoff hidden in this reduction.Translate  $z$  to the origin and apply a signed coordinate permutation sending the first frame to
$$s=N=(-1,0),\qquad d=E=(0,1).$$
Tags transform by the same linear map. The first active stencil is
$$(1,-1),\quad(0,-1),\quad(-1,-1),$$
all tagged  $N$ .I checked every nonbase row of the note’s table:Second frameSecond stencil supplying the overlapOverlapRequired second tag $(S,E)$ Active $(0,-1)$  $S$  $(S,W)$ Passive $(-1,-1)$  $W$  $(E,S)$ Active $(-1,-1)$  $E$  $(E,N)$ Active $(1,-1)$  $E$  $(N,W)$ Passive $(1,-1)$  $W$  $(W,S)$ Active $(-1,-1)$  $W$  $(W,N)$ Active $(1,-1)$  $W$ Every overlap has first tag  $N$  and a different second tag. There are exactly eight ordered perpendicular cardinal frames: four choices of  $s$ , followed by two perpendicular choices of  $d$ . Therefore only  $(N,E)$  survives.With equal  $z$  and equal frames,
$$p=z-s-d,\qquad q=z-s$$
are equal for the two contacts. Original endpoint ownership identifies the original ports, and their fixed neutral receiver identifies the same contact. The two terminals of one source cannot create an ambiguity here: they are different endpoint positions.This proves the asserted injection
$$\{\text{all actual neutral01 contacts}\}\longrightarrow \mathbb Z^2,
\qquad e\longmapsto z(e).$$
It applies simultaneously to contacts on closed components and open paths. It does not use an AA census, acyclicity, a source-count bound, or owner freshness.There is also a useful logical separation in the note: injectivity itself does not need the subsequent proof that  $z\in P$ . The stencil argument establishes injectivity of the geometrically defined positions. Support retention is needed to interpret those positions as forced original endpoints.2. as an inward support of the active source and an exterior support of the passive source. Its anchors are

$$p=(1,-1),\qquad q=(1,0),\qquad p-s=(2,-1).$$
The last point is the active port’s retained original support. These positions force the actual neutral receiver to be
$$Q_{\mathrm{neutral}}=\{1,2\}\times\{-1,0\}.$$
Therefore, in the transported physical partition, the adjacent tile containing  $z=(0,0)$  is
$$Q=\{-1,0\}\times\{-1,0\}.$$
Its corners are
$$p+s=(0,-1),\qquad
p+2s=(-1,-1),\qquad
z=(0,0),\qquad
z+s=(-1,0).$$
This is the tile asserted in the note.
